title: IO Graph: Add checkbox to prevent automatic rescans
description:
Adds a checkbox 'Prevent Rescan' to the IO Graph to disable rescans and
recalculation of graph data temporarily. This is usefull when you want to
modify settings of multiple graphs without triggering a rescan with every
change of a signale setting. This becomes usefull for large trace files
in particular because it can save a lot of waiting time.

Rescan or recalculation events are queued while 'Prevent Rescan' is active.
Unchecking 'Prevent Rescan' triggers the queued updates.

I'd prefer to reverse the logic and use something like "Automatically Update" or "Automatically Redraw".

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4046/diffs?diff_id=243137194&start_sha=5a3fe493db97886f40928c1c6f92c93ce7940d4b)

You don't need to add the translations, this is done automatically. So I would remove the corresponding files. Also, should this be a setting, which is stored in the preferences? As we do a retap every time we open a dialog it might be weird, but on the other hand, I think it would make sense. But in such a case, the setting should be ignored for the initial loading

> But in such a case, the setting should be ignored for the initial loading

I think this is done by the default which is automatic update = ON.

I did not persist the setting because it meets the current behaviour that the graphs gets plotted directly when the IO Graph gets opened. But you are right. Maybe it is better when the drawing of the graphs needs to be triggered explicitly.
In the first step I would go with the MR as it is now. A preference could be added later on easily.

This is not how this works. Please address the issues raised. We have no other setting which is reset upon opening the dialog, therefore a preference would be required. Also, please do not provide translations as those are generated automatically by using the tr macro
I will add a preference and will remove the translations.

> We have no other setting which is reset upon opening the dialog, therefore a preference would be required.

This is not true. Setting **Log Scale** is not persisted and is not set when opening the dialog.
That is correct. The difference here being is, that Log Scale might not always be applicable, which is why it is quite ok to be not persistent. On the other hand, lazy-loading will be used everytime

How about another idea: A Button instead of a checkbox that needs to be clicked explicitly to draw the graphs. By default the IO graph would not draw to graphs so you get the chance to change some settings after opening the IO graph.

Otherwise you would get a weird user experience. With a checkbox that persists its setting you depend if you can change settings after opening the IO graph on the last time you closed the IO graph. I think it would be typical that the checkox is checked because it is nessecary to draw the graphs. So if you want to change some settings next time you open the IO Graph you need to prepare it this time already for the next time.

The bigger issue here is the change in behavior between a lower version of Wireshark and this one. Most users would not expect to have to click another button. They may learn fast, but in the beginning it will blockade a lot of workflows. Therefore Wireshark has to continue to work out-of-the-box as it had in the past. Now, having a second option to disable automatic load is fine and if the user opts to permanently disables on opening the dialog, perfect. 

But for the majority of users, the behavior should not change.

A button would therefore be even more of an inconvenience.

IO Graph: Add checkbox to enable or disable automatic updates

Adds a checkbox 'Automatic Update' to the IO Graph to enable or disable
rescans and recalculation of graph data temporarily. This is usefull when
you want to modify settings of multiple graphs without triggering a rescan
with every change of a signale setting. This becomes usefull for large trace
files in particular because it can save a lot of waiting time.

Rescan or recalculation events are queued while 'Automatic Update' is not
active Unchecking 'Automatic Update' triggers the queued updates.
